title: Du lịch đại trà và bản sắc · Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some societies are considering limiting short-term holiday rentals in residential neighbourhoods. What problems could this create, and what measures could be taken to address them?
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: Holiday rentals can bring income to residents while gradually changing the supply and character of residential neighbourhoods. Uniform restrictions can remove residents' supplementary income without recovering much housing; enforcement should distinguish occasional home-sharing from large commercial portfolios.

Strict limits can remove useful income from residents who occasionally rent a spare room. Occasional home-sharing can help residents cover costs without permanently removing an entire dwelling from the rental market. Applying the same prohibition to that activity and to commercial portfolios may impose substantial personal losses while recovering little housing for long-term occupation. Occasional use of a spare room removes less long-term housing than converting an entire portfolio of residential flats into year-round visitor accommodation. A household renting a room during a short holiday may use the proceeds to meet housing costs while continuing to occupy the property throughout the year. Removing that income does not necessarily create another permanent home, so a blanket ban can impose a visible loss without delivering the housing benefit used to justify it.

Rules should distinguish occasional home-sharing from large-scale commercial conversion. Registration and portfolio checks can enforce the distinction between home-sharing and commercial conversion, preventing an occasional-host exception from sheltering large-scale operations. Registration should link properties to their actual operators, so a company cannot present many permanently rented flats as separate households occasionally sharing a spare room to evade commercial limits. A registration system should therefore record occupancy and the number of properties controlled by each operator, allowing enforcement to concentrate on residential stock genuinely converted into continuous commercial accommodation.

Overall, restrictions should track homes returned to residential use and neighbourhood viability, while distinguishing genuine home-sharing from commercial conversion rather than penalising both identically.

paragraphs.quote: Rules should distinguish occasional home-sharing from large-scale commercial conversion. Registration and portfolio checks can enforce the distinction between home-sharing and commercial conversion, preventing an occasional-host exception from sheltering large-scale operations. Registration should link properties to their actual operators, so a company cannot present many permanently rented flats as separate households occasionally sharing a spare room to evade commercial limits. A registration system should therefore record occupancy and the number of properties controlled by each operator, allowing enforcement to concentrate on residential stock genuinely converted into continuous commercial accommodation.
